render_evidence.note: The supplied files labeled desktop/tablet/mobile do not have desktop/tablet/mobile pixel widths. Re-capture at the intended QA viewport dimensions before fidelity acceptance. Findings below are limited to discrepancies still visually evident in the supplied captures.

corrections.issue: The implementation screenshots are not captured/exported at the intended QA viewport widths; the file labeled desktop is 367 px wide versus the 1024 px approved reference.
corrections.visual_evidence: Reference is 1024×1536. Supplied implementation files measure desktop 367×2048, tablet 293×2048, and mobile 104×2048. This prevents reliable desktop geometry comparison and makes breakpoint behavior ambiguous.
corrections.target: Produce browser screenshots at the project’s actual desktop/tablet/mobile QA viewport widths with no post-capture horizontal downscaling. Desktop must expose the desktop layout breakpoint and be directly comparable to the approved desktop reference.
corrections.implementation_guidance: Do not alter page styling merely to compensate for these narrow exported files. Correct the screenshot/capture procedure first, then use the corrected desktop render to verify layout.
corrections.verification: Image metadata matches intended QA viewport width and desktop render visibly activates desktop header, filter rail, and three-column collection layout.

corrections.issue: The implemented hero does not reproduce the approved image-led hero composition.
corrections.visual_evidence: Approved reference has mountain/road scenery across the hero, a large wheel/vehicle crop on the right, and the 'DRIVEN BY HIGHER STANDARDS' treatment. V1 renders show a mostly flat dark hero with text and no comparable dominant right-side wheel/scenic composition.
corrections.target: Match the approved hero hierarchy and visual mass: full-bleed scenic background, large right-side wheel/vehicle focal image, left text block, gold WHEELS emphasis, and right-side standards treatment, while retaining the shared Calder header/container system.
corrections.implementation_guidance: Correct Collection-specific hero assets/settings/layout. Do not redesign the global header or create a new cross-page design system.
corrections.verification: Corrected desktop render visibly matches the reference’s image-led hero composition and fitment transition.

corrections.region: Results region / filter rail / product grid
corrections.issue: The approved desktop architecture is not demonstrated: persistent left filter rail plus right-side three-column product grid.
corrections.visual_evidence: Approved reference clearly shows a persistent faceted sidebar and three product columns. The supplied V1 capture presents compact filter controls and a two-column/narrow product layout rather than the reference desktop structure.
corrections.target: At the true desktop QA breakpoint, render a persistent left filter sidebar and a right results area containing the toolbar and three B1 card columns. Pagination and help CTA must align to the results column, excluding the sidebar.
corrections.implementation_guidance: First re-capture at the correct desktop width. If the true desktop page still fails, correct Collection-specific grid/facet CSS and breakpoint behavior only. Preserve Shopify facet functionality and B1 internals.
corrections.verification: Desktop render shows the filter rail continuously at left and exactly three product columns at right with stable gaps and no B1 distortion.

corrections.issue: The complete approved Calder footer is not visibly rendered; a very large blank region follows the newsletter/benefits area.
corrections.visual_evidence: Approved reference transitions directly from newsletter/benefits into a full dark footer with logo, link columns, social icons, brand statement and legal row. V1 captures show newsletter/benefits followed by extensive white space with only faint Calder branding/rules.
corrections.target: Restore the accepted global footer immediately after the shared newsletter/benefits section with no abnormal blank page region.
corrections.implementation_guidance: Determine whether Collection-specific CSS/layout is hiding, recoloring, displacing or expanding the shared footer. Prefer removing Collection interference rather than editing the accepted footer itself.
corrections.verification: Corrected render shows the complete dark shared footer directly below newsletter/benefits and no excessive trailing whitespace.

corrections.issue: Fitment presentation is materially different from the approved compact desktop panel.
corrections.visual_evidence: Reference uses a heading/status row plus one horizontal row of YEAR, MAKE, MODEL, TRIM and a right-aligned FIND WHEELS CTA. V1 capture shows a smaller stacked/2×2 control arrangement and lacks the same selected-vehicle/reset presentation.
corrections.target: At desktop width, reproduce the approved compact single-row selector geometry and heading/status relationship while preserving the existing fitment engine.
corrections.implementation_guidance: Change Collection presentation/layout only; do not rewrite fitment data or event behavior.
corrections.verification: Desktop render shows four labeled selectors in one row plus CTA, with selected vehicle/reset state in the panel header.

corrections.issue: Category tiles lack the approved image-backed visual treatment and scale.
corrections.visual_evidence: Reference uses five wide photographic tiles with prominent white line icons and labels. V1 shows small pale/white tiles with minimal imagery and substantially less visual weight.
corrections.target: Reproduce five horizontal image-backed tiles with approved active gold accent, icon hierarchy, label placement, dark photographic surfaces and reference-like height/gaps.
corrections.implementation_guidance: Use Collection-specific tile settings/assets and styling; retain all five destinations and active-state logic.
corrections.verification: Desktop render presents five visually substantial image-backed tiles aligned across the shared container.

corrections.issue: The product cards do not visually resemble the approved Collection card presentation at the available width; existing Lumia controls/content dominate and image scale is excessive.
corrections.visual_evidence: Reference cards have controlled wheel-image scale, green fitment badge, concise C1/C2/C3-style hierarchy, finish/sizes/price, and dark View Details CTA. V1 cards show large cropped wheel imagery and multiple small legacy controls/labels that materially change card density.
corrections.target: Preserve the approved shared B1 internals while ensuring the Collection grid supplies the intended card width and does not expose conflicting legacy/Lumia presentation that is not part of B1.
corrections.implementation_guidance: Do not redesign B1. Verify that the collection is actually rendering the accepted B1 implementation and that collection CSS is not forcing a width/state that triggers incompatible legacy presentation.
corrections.verification: At corrected desktop width, B1 cards retain their approved internal hierarchy and fit cleanly in three columns without oversized imagery or conflicting legacy controls.

corrections.issue: The shared lower-page newsletter does not reproduce the approved scenic image-backed treatment.
corrections.visual_evidence: Reference newsletter is a scenic mountain band with horizontal email form and five benefit items. V1 renders show a dark flat band with a different visual density and fewer/stacked benefits at narrower captures.
corrections.target: Reuse the accepted Home newsletter/benefits presentation and assets so desktop matches the approved scenic horizontal band; responsive stacking may follow accepted shared behavior.
corrections.implementation_guidance: Verify section settings/assets and Collection CSS interference before modifying the shared component.
corrections.verification: Desktop shows the accepted scenic background, horizontal newsletter form and full benefits row; tablet/mobile remain usable without clipping.
